newsitem.title: USA: Death row dog earns calls for reprieve.
newsitem.headline: Death row dog earns calls for reprieve.

text.p: A Labrador retriever, awaiting execution for killing a rooster, has found a new champion calling for mercy -- the rooster's owner.

Portsmouth's animal control officers labeled the 3-year-old Labrador, named Prince, a vicious animal after he killed the rooster in May. The designation meant Prince had to be kept in a pen and be on a leash when he was walked.

But Prince escaped his cage twice and that brought him under the town's other dog control ordinance, which says that if a vicious animal escapes twice, it must be destroyed, according to Portsmouth police prosecutor Robert Ducharme.
However publicity surrounding Prince's plight brought calls for mercy not just from his owners, Margaret Kristiansen, and her son Jeffrey, 5, but also from the rooster's owner, Arthur Pearl.
"It's just a rooster," Pearl, 77, told Reuters. "What is the world coming to? The dog should be tied up. Killing him won't help me. It ain't right."
A court hearing was scheduled for Prince's owners for next Tuesday.
